findings.explanation: Applying the empty map with natural-number values gives 0 in Lean because the missing-key branch returns ARB, which reduces to the type’s default. In HOL4, every missing key gives OUTL (INR one). The saved equation for OUTL specifies only OUTL (INL x) = x, so HOL4 leaves the shared missing-key value open.
findings.repair:
private opaque missingFApplyValue (β : Type v) [Nonempty β] : β := Classical.choice inferInstance

def FAPPLY [Inhabited β] (f : FMap α β) (x : α) : β :=
  match f.lookup x with
  | some y => y
  | none => missingFApplyValue β
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.Prelude.FMap

example : HOL.FAPPLY (HOL.FEMPTY : HOL.FMap Nat Nat) 0 = 0 := rfl
findings.hol4_check: FAPPLY (FEMPTY : num |-> num) 0 = OUTL (INR one : num + one)

findings.explanation: Lean returns FEMPTY for every infinite P, so even FUN_FMAP (fun n : Nat => n) UNIV equals FEMPTY. HOL4 guards the entire FUN_FMAP specification with FINITE P. On the set of all natural numbers, any finite map satisfies that specification.
findings.repair:
private opaque infiniteFunFMap (f : α → β) (P : Set α) : FMap α β := FEMPTY

def FUN_FMAP (f : α → β) (P : Set α) : FMap α β :=
  if h : FINITE P then
    ⟨fun a => if a ∈ P then some (f a) else none,
     by
       obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := h
       refine ⟨l, fun a ha => ?_⟩
       by_cases hp : a ∈ P
       · exact hl a hp
       · simp [hp] at ha⟩
  else infiniteFunFMap f P
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.Prelude.FMap

open HOL

example (f : Nat → Nat) (P : HOL.Set Nat) (h : ¬ FINITE P) :
    FUN_FMAP f P = FEMPTY := by
  simp [FUN_FMAP, h]
findings.hol4_check: !f P k. FINITE P ==> (FLOOKUP (FUN_FMAP f P) k = if k IN P then SOME (f k) else NONE)
